stem: P and Q are married to each other and have exactly two children, R and S, of whom R is the only son. R is married to T, and U is the only child of R and T. Q is the brother of V. How is the grandmother of U related to V?

per_option_rationale.rationale: U's parents are R and T; R's parents are the couple P and Q, so U's grandmother is whichever of P and Q is female. Q is the brother of V, so Q is male, forcing P to be the female of the couple and hence U's grandmother. P is Q's wife and V is Q's brother, so P, a woman, is V's sister-in-law.
Mother-in-law places P one generation above V; but P and V belong to the same generation (P married V's brother), so the in-law tie is sibling-level, not parental.
Sister treats P as a blood sibling of V; P is related to V only by marriage to V's brother Q, so the relation is sister-in-law, not sister.

Aunt would follow from reading the grandmother as Q's generation parent or mis-gendering the chain; here the grandmother is P, same generation as V, so the term is the in-law peer term, sister-in-law.

explanation: First find U's grandmother. U is the child of R and T, and R is a child of the couple P and Q, so U's grandparents on this side are P and Q; the grandmother is the female one. The gender is not stated directly: it is forced through Q. Q is the brother of V, so Q is male; since P and Q are a married couple they are opposite in gender, so P is female and is therefore U's grandmother. Now relate P to V. P is the wife of Q, and V is the brother of Q, so P is the spouse of V's sibling. The spouse of one's sibling is a brother-in-law or sister-in-law; since P is female, P is V's sister-in-law.

explanation_sections.punchline: U's grandmother is the female of the couple P and Q; Q is male because he is V's brother, so P is the grandmother, and as the wife of V's brother she is V's sister-in-law.
explanation_sections.approach: Archetype move: when a relation's gender is never stated, fix it indirectly through a sibling or spouse whose gender a word like brother or wife reveals, then propagate it across the married couple before naming the final in-law term.
explanation_sections.lesson: A married couple is gender-opposite; one explicit gendered word anywhere in the couple's network determines both partners and unlocks every dependent term.
explanation_sections.timing: 120-150 seconds. Fastest elimination: Mother-in-law dies once you see P and V share a generation through marriage, ruling out any parental in-law term.
